children: Deere & Co. (DE) stock edged higher overnight as CEO John May signaled that the agricultural equipment downturn “troughed” in fiscal 2026, setting the stage for a 2027 recovery. North America could lead the rebound, while aging machinery in Brazil and continued data center investments offer additional growth opportunities.
inched 0.5% higher overnight on Wednesday, after a 4% rally in the regular session.
Deere Says Agriculture Recovery To Gain Momentum In 2027
Speaking during the fourth-quarter (Q4) earnings call, Deere CEO John May said the company’s businesses experienced different operating environments during fiscal 2026.

“In large Ag, farmers are still working through tight margins, increasing input costs and volatile commodity markets. In construction, markets kept getting stronger with infrastructure and rental fleet investments supporting strong order books.”
Looking toward fiscal 2027, May said, “The ag equipment cycle troughed in 2026. The proof points from our early order programs point to North America leading the global recovery.”

He also pointed to an aging machinery base and insufficient inventories of new equipment as factors that could encourage farmers to replace older machines. These purchases could continue even while agricultural customers contend with challenging financial conditions.
Brazil, Data Centers Could Provide Additional Growth For Deere

Deere sees opportunities for stronger performance than its current outlook suggests, prompting the company to provide a broader sales outlook for the coming year. “The upside depends on filling out the remainder of our North American order book at the pace similar to our early order programs,” said May.

“Or the other option that could happen is on a back-end loaded recovery in Brazil, where aging fleet dynamics are building rapidly due to a machine usage intensity that is twice the level of North America.”
The company
to earn $4.5 billion to $5.25 billion in fiscal 2027, below analysts' estimate of $5.91 billion. In Q4, Deere’s earnings per share (EPS) of $3.89, missed Street’s view of $4.01.

Beyond agriculture, May identified North American earthmoving equipment as another area showing strength. Demand in this business has gained support from expanding data center construction and related infrastructure investments.
DE Stock: Retail View
On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the stock improved to ‘extremely bullish’ from ‘bullish’ with a 392% increase in message volume over the past 24 hours.
A user
, “This stock is showing a lot more character than I expected.”
DE stock has gained 37% year-to-date.
Deere CEO expects the agricultural equipment market to recover in 2027, led by North America.
The company sees a possible recovery in Brazil, where aging equipment could drive replacements.
However, Deere’s fiscal 2027 net income fell short of expectations.

title: DE Stock Ticks Higher Overnight: Deere CEO Sees Agriculture Recovery In 2027 — Brazil And Data Centers Could Add To The Upside
